# HIL — Hardware-in-the-Loop testing for lab instruments

> HIL (hil-harness) is a Python hardware-in-the-loop testing harness that drives
> lab instruments — SCPI devices plus power profilers, logic analyzers and
> on-chip flash/debug probes — from one Python API, one CLI and one MCP server,
> with a safety policy on every device profile.

- Repository: https://github.com/adwuard/HIL
- Site: https://hsuanhanlai.com/HIL/
- License: MIT · Version: 0.1.0 · Python 3.10+ · Author: Hsuan Han Lai

## Facts

- Corpus: 725 instruments, 7 vendors, ~294k SCPI commands (Keysight 279, Rigol 211, Keithley 85, Tektronix 84, EA 29, Rohde & Schwarz 22, B&K 15).
- Eight curated profiles load by default with safety policies: keithley-2400, rigol-dho1072, keysight-ac6801b, ea-el9000b, nordic-ppk2, alientek-atk-logic, generic-cortex-m, esp32-devkit.
- Drivers: scpi, ppk2 (Nordic Power Profiler Kit II), logic (ALIENTEK ATK-Logic), debug (probe-rs, pyOCD, OpenOCD, esptool, stlink).
- Debug loop: one agent command builds the firmware, flashes it over the probe (SWD on Cortex-M, UART on ESP32), halts and single-steps, spools RTT and memory dumps as artifacts, then hands the running DUT to an instrument sequence; a failed assertion reopens the build with the capture attached.
- Addressing: tcp://, serial://, visa://, ppk2://, logic://, debug:// or a registry slug.
- Safety by default: each profile carries a policy (block / allow / limits); the bench refuses blocked commands.
- Simulator: dry-run any YAML procedure with `hil bench run <plan>.yaml --sim`; validate statically with `hil bench validate`.
- Agent-ready: every CLI command emits stable `--json`; the MCP server exposes hil_doctor, hil_devices, hil_device, hil_probe, hil_exec, hil_errors, hil_capture, hil_debug_probe, hil_debug, hil_setup. Every tool returns JSON with an `ok` flag.

## Install

```
pip install git+https://github.com/adwuard/HIL.git
pip install 'hil-harness[mcp]'   # MCP server extra
hil mcp install                  # register with your coding agent
hil doctor                       # bench readiness
hil setup <slug>                 # provision an optional backend, e.g. ppk2
```

Extras: .[serial] .[visa] .[atk] .[ppk2] .[mcp] .[all] .[dev]

## Quick start

```
from hil import connect
smu = connect("keithley-2400")          # registry slug -> safety policy attached
print(smu.query(":MEAS:VOLT?"))
```

```
hil idn tcp://192.168.1.5:5025          # identify
hil ask keithley-2400 ":MEAS:VOLT?"     # query (safety-checked)
hil bench run plan.yaml --sim           # dry-run on the simulator
```
